prompt: Mailvora's marketing manager asked whether the GA4 export and the backend agree on sessions for 1 to 7 December 2025. The check returned one row per Dublin day, with a difference of 0 on every day. Which summary states the grain of the numbers and a caveat the manager can act on?

options.text: Sessions agree between the export and the backend, so the GA4 numbers are right and can go into the board deck as they are, with no notes needed.

Each figure is one Dublin day of sessions, a session being one visitor with one session ID; the export and the backend agree on all seven days. Caveat: about 2% of sessions come from visitors who denied consent, so the export cannot link them to a visitor.

Sessions match on every day of the week, one row per Dublin day, and the check shows the difference between the export and the backend is 0 each time, which is what we expected from a correct tag and a correct backend count, so there is nothing further to report.
Tracking looks healthy this week and the numbers tie out. One caveat: some visitors deny consent, so treat the GA4 visitor counts with some care before any campaign decision is made on them.
